name: Blog article
summary: The ahaslides.com blog post page, built from the DS: a post header (title, category tag, author, date and read time, an optional hero image), the article body that styles plain CMS HTML (headings, paragraphs, lists, quote, figure and caption, code, table and a callout), the aha-text-link class for links in a sentence, a table of contents that sticks beside the article on desktop and folds into a button on a phone, and a share row. The Article page layout puts them together with the article column capped at 720px. Framework-free and bound to the shared --aha-* tokens.
highlights: Built from what the WordPress blog export (headlesswp cli/wp-export) needed, so its token-built post skin can swap to these classes

Article body styles unclassed CMS HTML inside aha-article-prose: h2 to h4, p, ul and ol (nested), blockquote with cite, figure with figcaption, inline code and pre, table in aha-article-prose__table, hr, and the aha-article-callout panel
Type ramp from the DS scale only: title 48, 40 at 991px, 32 at 479px; body h2 32, h3 24, h4 20, one step down at 767px; body text 16 at line height 1.5; meta and captions 14

aha-text-link copies the Button text-link inline values: #DB005B, weight 400, underlined at rest, the 2px Vivid Pink ring outside a 2px gap; inside a quote or callout a link is the default ink, since pink links sit on white only (colour rule 6.6)

Table of contents: sticky in the 384px column beside the article from 992px, a secondary Button that opens and closes the list below 992px; a link with aria-current="location" shows the section being read in Vivid Pink (a selection, colour rule 6.9). The page sets it (server side or from lib/marketing-motion.js once it offers a section spy): W9 allows no hand-written scroll script, so the section ships no observer

Share row: tertiary icon-only Buttons with the Brand icons brand-linkedin, brand-x and brand-facebook (colour rule 2.6a, icon ink, hover follows the Button), each opening in a new tab, and a Copy link Button that says Link copied in a status line
Category and post tags are aha-tag inside a link; the category sits in the meta row under the title, because W14 allows no label above a heading
The hero image and figures are real img elements at their own ratio, never cropped (W6); until a picture exists they are the DS image placeholder
Spacing uses the section spacing levels and the page gutter (64, 24 at 767px, 16 at 479px); checked at 1280, 768 and 375px
layoutsIntro: Article page is the whole post: use it for a blog post. The other layouts are its parts, each shown on its own so you can see every state; they share one stylesheet, so a page that pastes Article page has them all.

composedOf.use: Category tag (color primary) and post tags (neutral), each inside a link
Author avatar in the meta row: size small (24), initials until the author photo is set
Share and Copy link (tertiary, icon-only, lg), the table of contents toggle (secondary, lg, block) and the callout call to action (primary, xl)
brand-linkedin, brand-x, brand-facebook, system-link, system-caret-down and system-caret-up, 16px
aha-text-link copies the Button text-link variant at size inline
aha-tag has no href form or hover state, so a category or post tag link shows only the focus ring on its wrapping link; stand-in: aha-tag inside an a.aha-article-tag

layouts.name: Article page
layouts.summary: The whole blog post: post header across the top, then the table of contents and share row in a sticky 384px column beside the 720px article body, and the post tags under the body. Below 992px it is one column: header, the folded table of contents, share row, body, tags.
layouts.useFor: A blog post page. Paste it once per post and fill the header, the body HTML from the CMS and the table of contents from its h2 and h3 ids.

How to run a team quiz people actually want to join

Team building Leah Nguyen ·5 November 2026·6 min read
On this page

On this page

  1. Start with a warm-up
    1. Keep the first question low stakes
  2. Keep each round short
  3. Mix your question types
    1. Which type fits which moment
  4. Share the quiz on your intranet
  5. Wrap up with the results

Share

A good team quiz feels like a break, not a test. In this guide you’ll set one up in about ten minutes, keep everyone playing to the last question and finish with results people want to talk about. New to live quizzes? Read what a live quiz is first.

Start with a warm-up

The first minute decides whether people lean in or reach for their inbox. Open with a question anyone can answer, and show the live results straight away so the room sees itself on screen.

Keep the first question low stakes

  • Ask for an opinion, not a fact: “Tea or coffee?” beats a capital city.
  • Leave scoring off for the warm-up, so nobody starts the quiz behind.
  • Give a short timer, then talk through the answers:
    • call out the most popular answer
    • thank the one brave outlier

Keep each round short

Five to seven questions a round is plenty. Between rounds, show the leaderboard and give people a moment to cheer or groan.

  1. Pick a theme for each round.
  2. Write the questions, then cut the two weakest.
  3. Add one picture question to every round.

We swapped our monthly all-hands icebreaker for a three-round quiz. Attendance went up, and people stayed for the updates too.

Mai Tran, People team lead

Mix your question types

Multiple choice is quick to play, but a whole quiz of it gets flat. Change the type every few questions to keep the pace up.

Which type fits which moment

Question typeBest forTime to play
Pick answerFast facts and warm-ups20 seconds
Type answerRecall without hints30 seconds
Match pairsLinking terms to meanings45 seconds
Correct orderTimelines and steps45 seconds

Share the quiz on your intranet

Remote colleagues can join from a page they already use. Paste the embed code into any page that accepts HTML, and replace your-code with your presentation’s access code.

<iframe src="https://ahaslides.com/your-code" width="100%" height="600" title="Team quiz"></iframe>

Wrap up with the results

End on the final leaderboard, then thank everyone by name. Export the results afterwards to see which questions caught people out.

layouts.name: Table of contents
layouts.summary: An ordered list of the article’s h2 and h3 links under an On this page title. From 992px it shows open, and inside Article page it sticks beside the article; below 992px it folds behind an On this page Button that opens and closes the list. Set aria-current="location" on the link of the section being read to mark it in Vivid Pink; the section itself never watches the scroll (W9).
layouts.useFor: Any article with three or more h2 sections.

layouts.name: Share row
layouts.summary: A Share label, LinkedIn, X and Facebook share links that open in a new tab, and a Copy link Button that copies data-url (or the page address) and says Link copied in a status line for 3 seconds.
layouts.useFor: Sharing a blog post or another public page. Set data-url and the url parameter of each share link to the page address.
